name: Real REMAX Group Inc.

profile.description: Real REMAX Group Inc. (formerly The Real Brokerage Inc., renamed August 2026 following its acquisition of RE/MAX Holdings) is a real estate technology company operating a tech-native, agent-first brokerage model across the United States and Canada. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Miami, Florida, the company provides title, mortgage, digital wallet, and franchising/ancillary services alongside its core brokerage platform, reZEN, which uses AI-powered tools to reduce agents' administrative burden.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): Real completed a transformative $880 million all-stock-and-cash acquisition of RE/MAX Holdings in 2026, rebranding as Real REMAX Group and vaulting into the top five U.S. brokerages by agent count and sales volume, while FY2025 revenue surged 56% to $2.0 billion and net loss narrowed to just $8.1 million [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): The proprietary reZEN platform embeds AI-powered tools designed to reduce agent administrative work, per CEO Tamir Poleg's stated strategy of pursuing 'pure tech innovation' rather than reworking the legacy commission model [4][5]. Market Share (2/2): The company surpassed 35,000 agents (+26% YoY) and ranks among the five largest U.S. brokerages by the 2025 RealTrends Verified Brokerage Rankings, with Q2 2026 revenue of $700.6 million (+30% YoY) [3][4]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Ancillary services (title, mortgage origination, escrow, fintech wallet) plus RE/MAX franchising integration create a multi-year cross-sell roadmap, with combined pro forma adjusted EBITDA of ~$190 million including $30M of committed synergies [8]. R&D Intensity (1/1): The tech-native virtual brokerage model requires sustained platform investment in reZEN to support its rapid agent-count scaling.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Real's agent-first ethos is built around helping agents build long-term wealth through a collaborative, transparent revenue-share model, which is a real point of differentiation from traditional franchise brokerages but not uniquely distinctive versus other agent-centric platforms like eXp Realty [4][6]. Community Impact (0/2): No specific community investment or philanthropic program was identified in the research window. Employee/Agent Retention (2/2): The company promoted three former agents into senior roles in 2026 — Ken Pozek to the Board, Dusty Oglesby as VP of Agent Learning and Development, and Jason Cassity as Chief Growth Officer — explicitly to 'strengthen agent voice in executive leadership,' and 26% YoY agent-count growth suggests strong agent satisfaction driving organic recruitment [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying was identified.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics as a Growth stock. REAX shows explosive top-line momentum with revenue growth YoY of 29.6% and an approximate 3-year revenue CAGR (2022-2025, the longest window available) of roughly 73%, both scoring at or above target and carrying full weight under the algorithm [1][9]. However, profitability metrics remain a drag: ROE of -24.9% and profit margin of -0.72% both sit at or below the zero floor, reflecting the company's continued investment phase (agent commission payouts and stock-based comp) even as GAAP losses have narrowed sharply year over year [1][9]. Forward P/E and PEG are not meaningful given negative near-term forward earnings following the RE/MAX acquisition, and debt-to-equity was unavailable from source data. Liquidity comfortably clears the floor at roughly $12.5 million in average daily dollar volume ($19.02 x ~655K shares).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Real's tech-native, low-overhead virtual brokerage model is structurally better positioned than legacy franchise competitors to absorb AI-driven changes to real estate search and lead generation, since its cost base and agent economics were designed around software leverage from inception rather than physical office footprints [4][5]. Some residual risk exists from portal operators (e.g., Zillow) building AI concierge and matching tools that could compress buy-side commissions industry-wide, a risk shared across the brokerage sector post-NAR settlement. AI Opportunity Tiebreaker (1/1): reZEN's AI-powered agent tools are already reducing administrative overhead in production, giving Real a genuine efficiency and margin-expansion lever as it integrates RE/MAX's franchise network [4][5].

infinite_game.summary: Real REMAX Group displays strong existential flexibility and trusting-teams evidence through its bold RE/MAX acquisition and agent-to-leadership promotions, anchored by a genuine (if not fully distinctive) agent-wealth-building cause; the main gap is limited public evidence of community investment or courage-tested crisis response beyond aggressive market expansion.

just_cause.analysis: Real's stated purpose of helping agents build long-term wealth through revenue share and equity, rather than maximizing near-term commission extraction, gives it a genuine cause beyond quarterly transaction volume, though the pitch is shared by other agent-centric platforms like eXp Realty [4][6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Completing an $880 million acquisition of RE/MAX — a much larger, century-old legacy franchise brand — while still posting a net loss shows willingness to make a bold, dilutive long-horizon bet rather than optimize for near-term profitability [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Elevating three former agents into the Board, VP of Agent Learning and Development, and Chief Growth Officer roles is concrete evidence of distributing real decision-making authority to the frontline rather than concentrating it at the executive layer [4].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Rather than deepening its pure-play discount brokerage model, Real is diversifying into title, mortgage, fintech wallet, and now full-service franchising via RE/MAX — a substantive strategic pivot to diversify revenue beyond commission splits ahead of industry disruption [1][8].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Real operates in a fiercely competitive field against Compass, eXp Realty, Zillow, and traditional franchise brokerages, and its response — aggressive agent recruitment plus the RE/MAX acquisition — treats rivalry as a spur for structural differentiation rather than price competition alone [4].

investment_thesis: Real REMAX Group is the fastest-growing major U.S. brokerage, having scaled to 35,000+ agents and $2.0 billion of FY2025 revenue (+56%) on a tech-native, low-overhead model, and it just completed a transformative $880 million acquisition of RE/MAX that adds a century-old global franchise brand and ~$190 million of pro forma combined adjusted EBITDA including committed synergies [1][2][8]. The agent-first culture — reinforced by promoting former agents into the Board and C-suite — has driven strong organic recruitment and narrowing losses even as the company continues to invest in AI-enabled tools (reZEN) and ancillary revenue streams (title, mortgage, fintech wallet) [4][5].
thesis_continued: The core risk is that Infrastructure metrics remain weak on a mechanical basis: ROE and profit margin are still negative as the company absorbs RE/MAX integration costs and continues to fund rapid agent-count growth, and forward earnings visibility is limited immediately post-acquisition. Investors are effectively underwriting continued execution of the RE/MAX integration and a path to sustained profitability, which is plausible given the trajectory of narrowing losses and rising adjusted EBITDA, but is not yet proven at scale.
key_catalysts: RE/MAX integration synergies (targeted $30M committed run-rate) flowing through to consolidated adjusted EBITDA over 2026-2027
Continued agent-count growth (+26% YoY) expanding the revenue base and ancillary service attach rates (title, mortgage, wallet)
Path to sustained GAAP profitability as losses have narrowed from prior years toward breakeven
key_risks: Integration execution risk from absorbing RE/MAX's legacy franchise network and culture into a tech-native brokerage model
Industry-wide commission compression risk from AI-enabled portal search/matching tools and post-NAR-settlement buyer-agent fee pressure
Persistently negative ROE and profit margin under the mechanical Infrastructure scoring, reflecting an unproven path to durable profitability
